response.sql: WITH per_status AS (SELECT COALESCE(CENTROMEA, 'missing') AS status, AVG(GOT - GPT) AS avg_ast_minus_alt, AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 GROUP BY COALESCE(CENTROMEA, 'missing')) SELECT AVG(avg_ast_minus_alt) AS avg_ast_minus_alt, AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM per_status;

assumptions.assumption: Only SQL NULL in CENTROMEA marks a missing status; empty or whitespace-only strings are treated as their own status, not as missing.

Each record's differences are computed row by row. AVG ignores NULL differences, so records missing GOT, GPT, APTT, or PT are skipped for the relevant average, and a status whose average is NULL is dropped from the final average.
Lab rows are used as-is; the (ID, Date) primary key means each row is one lab record, so no deduplication is applied.
